title: Cloud metadata address written with a trailing root dot
description: Tests blocking of a request to the link-local cloud metadata address when the host is written with a trailing dot. URL parsers that follow the URL Standard drop the empty final label and connect to the same address, so a control that compares the host as written never matches it.
notes: Same path as ssrf-cloud-metadata-007; only the host spelling differs. The trailing dot marks an absolute name and adds an empty final label, which a canonicalizing parser removes before it treats the host as an IPv4 address. A control must reach its decision on the canonical host, not on the string as written. Pairs with ssrf-benign-trailing-dot-host-016, which uses the same spelling on an allowed host so that refusing every trailing-dot host fails the companion instead of passing this case.
source: WHATWG URL Standard, IPv4 parser (a trailing empty part is removed); RFC 1034 section 3.1 (absolute domain names end in the root label)
